profile.reading:
Csquare ORD1 sits at 350 East Cermak Road, Chicago, Illinois 60616, occupying the 4th, 7th, and 8th floors of an eight-story building in Chicago's South Loop financial district, roughly 30 minutes from O'Hare and 25 minutes from Midway airports. This address is one of the best-known carrier-hotel and multi-tenant data center buildings in the United States, historically home to numerous colocation operators across its many floors. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, launched April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business under Brookfield since 2019) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's own spec page states 58,893 square feet of raised floor at ORD1, closely matching its SEC Form S-1 property table, which splits the site into two leased assets, ORD1_A at 33,032 square feet (51.1 percent leased) and ORD1_B at 26,191 square feet (91.1 percent leased), summing to 59,223 square feet as of March 31, 2026. Csquare states 32.8 megawatts of utility power, 8.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 16 megawatts of generator capacity for ORD1, with SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 compliance certifications. Csquare does not name a power utility or a year-opened date for ORD1 on its current site.

350 East Cermak Road is one of the most significant carrier-hotel and multi-tenant data center buildings in North America, historically hosting dozens of colocation, cloud, and network operators across its many floors since the building's original telecom-hub development in the 1990s. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, with ORD1 representing one of three Csquare-branded footholds within Chicago's broader, highly competitive data center market alongside ORD2 and ORD4.

This session found that centersquaredc.com, the legacy domain matching this registry entire Centersquare operator bucket naming, now issues a live redirect to www.csquare.com, the operator current domain, confirmed directly this session. Csquare own site states it owns and operates data centers built over decades by developing, acquiring, integrating, and operating advanced data centers, without giving a specific founding or rebrand date on the pages fetched this session. Csquare own site, fetched this session, lists corporate headquarters at 3100 Olympus Blvd, Suite 510, Coppell, TX 75019, and states a current portfolio of 80 total data centers, about 3.5 million square feet, more than 500 MW of power capacity, and more than 36,000 cross connects, across 15 North American markets plus London. On at least two Csquare pages fetched this session, a customer facing portal link pointed to evoquedcs.my.site.com, suggesting some relationship to Evoque Data Center Solutions, though this session found no page stating the exact nature of that relationship, such as whether Centersquare or Csquare is a direct rebrand of Evoque or a separate successor. Separately, this registry also carries an unrelated Cyxtera operator bucket, not part of this batch, already documented by an earlier pass in this registry as tracing to the same May 2017 CenturyLink data center divestiture discussed in this session own Lumen Technologies research, and as acquired by Cologix in 2023 per Cologix own site. This session found no evidence connecting that Cyxtera and Cologix history to the Centersquare, Csquare, or Evoque names researched for this batch, so the two threads are treated as distinct and unconfirmed to be related. This registry also carries a separate Csquare operator bucket, not part of this batch, whose name is now confirmed by the redirect evidence above to very likely be the same current brand as the Centersquare bucket this batch covers, though this session did not merge or rename either bucket, flagging this as an open duplicate operator naming question for a future dedicated pass rather than resolving it unilaterally. The operator own current market page for Chicago, fetched this session, describes this facility as Chicago Cermak ORD1 and states 32.8 MW of utility power and 58,893 square feet of raised floor, with no street address published on that page.

reading.body:
The Centersquare Chicago facility publishes 147.6 MW of utility power across 237,000 square feet of technical space, enough for roughly 3,700 racks at typical AI training density.

Centersquare operates 80 data centers across 15 North American markets claiming more than 500 MW total capacity. The Chicago facility holds security certifications for regulated financial, healthcare, and US government workloads, which limits its fungibility for commercial AI training but signals buildout for high-assurance compute. The operator's portfolio footprint matters for grid pressure because if the 500 MW claim is accurate, a single private operator controls meaningful regional power in multiple markets simultaneously.

A critical gap undermines any read of this facility's actual role in AI scaling. The operator publishes two different power figures for the same site: 147.6 MW in one location and 32.8 MW in another. The corresponding floor space figures do not reconcile either. Without third-party grid data or physical verification, it is impossible to determine whether this campus ranks among the largest compute buildouts in Illinois or among the smaller ones. This data shows that operator-published capacity figures remain unverified in real time, which matters because AI scaling constraints depend on actual grid load, not claimed nameplate.
